mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time over a 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 4% but S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase, it indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and increasing S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) leads to higher borrowing costs, reducing corporate investments and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) erodes purchasing power, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates reduced supply, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO is below 100 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) increase, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 25% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weak demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.
